questions.question: Statements: X ≥ Y < Z = A > B ≤ C Conclusions: I. X > B II. Y ≤ A III. Z ≥ C Which of the above conclusions are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Statements:
X ≥ Y < Z = A > B ≤ C
Conclusions:
I. X > B
II. Y ≤ A
III. Z ≥ C
Which of the above conclusions are correct?
questions.solution:
Statements:
X ≥ Y < Z = A > B ≤ C

X ≥ Y, but Y may be less than B → X > B not sure ✘

From Y < Z = A → Y < A → Y ≤ A not sure ✘

A > B ≤ C → no fixed relation between A (Z) and C ✘

Correct Conclusion: None of these

questions.solution:

A + 5 = F

I + 8 = Q ≠ P

questions.solution:
The oldest mountain range in India is the Aravalli Range.

The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world, formed during the Precambrian era.

In contrast, the Himalayas are geologically young fold mountains.

Western Ghats and Satpura Range are not as old as the Aravallis in geological terms.

options.text: Why was such a scathing letter written by your brother?

options.text: Why is such a scathing letter being written by your brother?

options.html: Why such a scathing letter was written by your brother?

questions.solution:
✅ Correct Answer: Why was such a scathing letter written by your brother?

Explanation: The active sentence is in simple past tense (did write). The correct passive form is was written, and the interrogative word order is properly maintained.

Why other options are incorrect:
Option 2 (is being written) is in present continuous tense, which changes the tense of the original sentence.
Option 3 (had been written) is in past perfect tense, which is not present in the original sentence.
Option 4 has incorrect interrogative word order; in passive questions, the auxiliary verb should come before the subject.

questions.question: Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: P: He was so tired that he fell asleep almost immediately. Q: After a long day of hiking through the rugged terrain of the Himalayas. R: The warmth of the campfire provided a much-needed respite from the biting cold. S: Rahul finally reached the base camp just as the sun was setting.
questions.questionHtml:
Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:

P: He was so tired that he fell asleep almost immediately.

Q: After a long day of hiking through the rugged terrain of the Himalayas.

R: The warmth of the campfire provided a much-needed respite from the biting cold.
S: Rahul finally reached the base camp just as the sun was setting.
questions.solution:
Correct Order

Q → S → R → P (QSRP) ✅

Why other options are wrong

QPRS: Jumps from background (Q) straight to sleep (P), skipping the natural sequence of reaching camp and enjoying the fire.

RQSP: Starts with the campfire (R) before explaining how Rahul got there; feels abrupt.

RSPQ: Begins with campfire (R), then reaching camp (S), then sleep (P), and ends with background (Q); completely disordered.

Let’s solve this step by step:

Start with Q → “After a long day of hiking through the rugged terrain of the Himalayas.” This sets the background and introduces the situation.

Next is S → “Rahul finally reached the base camp just as the sun was setting.” This completes the thought begun in Q, showing the result of the long day.

Then R → “The warmth of the campfire provided a much-needed respite from the biting cold.” This logically follows after reaching the camp, describing the comfort he found.

Finally P → “He was so tired that he fell asleep almost immediately.” This concludes the sequence with Rahul’s exhaustion and rest.

questions.question: Convert the following Complex sentence into a Simple sentence: "Since he was ill, he could not attend the summit."
questions.questionHtml:
Convert the following Complex sentence into a Simple sentence:

"Since he was ill, he could not attend the summit."

options.text: He being ill, he could not attend the summit.
options.html: He being ill, he could not attend the summit.

options.text: Because of his illness, he could not attend the summit.
options.html: Because of his illness, he could not attend the summit.

options.text: He was ill and so he did not attend the summit.
options.html: He was ill and so he did not attend the summit.

options.text: His illness prevented him to attend the summit.
options.html: His illness prevented him to attend the summit.

questions.solution:
Correct Answer:
Option 2 – Because of his illness, he could not attend the summit.

Explanation:

A simple sentence uses a phrase instead of a clause.

“Because of his illness” is a prepositional phrase replacing the dependent clause “Since he was ill,” making it a correct simple sentence.

Why other options are incorrect:

Option 1: Grammatically faulty due to repetition (“He being ill, he…”).

Option 3: This is a compound sentence (joined by and), not a simple sentence.

Option 4: Incorrect construction — it should be “prevented him from attending”, not “prevented him to attend”.

questions.question: Change the narration of the following sentence: The diplomat said to the press, "I will not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement has been signed by both the nations."
questions.questionHtml:
Change the narration of the following sentence:

The diplomat said to the press, "I will not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement has been signed by both the nations."

options.text: The diplomat told the press that he would not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement had been signed by both the nations.
options.html: The diplomat told the press that he would not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement had been signed by both the nations.

options.text: The diplomat said to the press that I will not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement was signed by both the nations.
options.html: The diplomat said to the press that I will not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement was signed by both the nations.

options.text: The diplomat informed the press that he will not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement had been signed by both the nations.
options.html: The diplomat informed the press that he will not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement had been signed by both the nations.

options.text: The diplomat told the press that he would not have commented on the negotiations until a formal agreement was signed.
options.html: The diplomat told the press that he would not have commented on the negotiations until a formal agreement was signed.

questions.solution:
Correct Answer:
The diplomat told the press that he would not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement had been signed by both the nations.

Explanation:
This option correctly changes direct to indirect speech:

“said to” → “told”

“I” → “he”

Future tense “will not comment” → “would not comment”

Present perfect “has been signed” → past perfect “had been signed”

Why the other options are incorrect:

Option 2: The diplomat said to the press that I will not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement was signed by both the nations.
Incorrect because the pronoun “I” is not changed to “he”, the tense “will not comment” is not back-shifted to “would not comment”, and “said to” should change to “told”.

Option 3: The diplomat informed the press that he will not comment on the ongoing negotiations until a formal agreement had been signed by both the nations.
Incorrect because “will not comment” should change to “would not comment” in indirect speech. There is also an inconsistency between “will” and “had been signed”.

Option 4: The diplomat told the press that he would not have commented on the negotiations until a formal agreement was signed.
Incorrect because “would not have commented” expresses a past hypothetical situation, which changes the original meaning. The original sentence refers to a future condition, not an unreal past action.

questions.question: Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: P: This shift is driven by the rapid advancement in Generative AI, which can now automate creative tasks previously thought to be uniquely human. questions.solution:

Start with R: “The global labor market is currently experiencing a seismic shift…”

Sets the broad context and introduces the main topic.

Next P: “This shift is driven by the rapid advancement in Generative AI…”

Explains the cause of the shift, logically following R.

Then Q: “However, this automation also raises significant ethical concerns…”

Introduces the key challenges and tensions arising from P.

Finally S: “Therefore, policymakers must balance the benefits…”

Provides a policy response and conclusion, naturally following the concerns in Q.

questions.question: If an angle is 20° more than three times its complement, find the measure of the angle.
questions.questionHtml: If an angle is 20° more than three times its complement, find the measure of the angle.
questions.solution:
Let the angle = x°

Complement = 90 − x

Given condition:
x = 3(90 − x) + 20

x = 270 − 3x + 20
x = 290 − 3x

4x = 290
x = 72.5°

questions.question: What is the minimum number of cuts required to divide a cuboid into 18 equal cuboids, if each cut must be straight and pass completely through the cuboid?
questions.questionHtml: What is the minimum number of cuts required to divide a cuboid into 18 equal cuboids, if each cut must be straight and pass completely through the cuboid?
questions.solution:
To divide a cuboid into equal cuboids, factorise the number.

18 = 2 × 3 × 3

Minimum cuts required
= (2 − 1) + (3 − 1) + (3 − 1)

questions.question: The highest common factor (HCF) of 84, 126, and a number b is 14. What is the least common multiple (LCM) of 84, 126, and b?
questions.questionHtml: The highest common factor (HCF) of 84, 126, and a number b is 14. What is the least common multiple (LCM) of 84, 126, and b?
questions.solution:
HCF of 84, 126 and b = 14
⇒ b must be a multiple of 14
For minimum / standard value, take b = 14

Prime factors:
84 = 2² × 3 × 7
126 = 2 × 3² × 7
14 = 2 × 7

LCM = highest powers of all primes
= 2² × 3² × 7
= 4 × 9 × 7
= 252

questions.questionHtml: A certain sum was to be divided between X and Y in the ratio of 7 : 5. However, by mistake, it was divided in the ratio of 5 : 7. Due to this mistake, X received ₹ 2,400 less than his original share. Find the total sum.
questions.solution:
Correct ratio = 7 : 5

Wrong ratio = 5 : 7

Difference in shares of X per unit

= (7 − 5) / (7 + 5)

= 2 / 12

Given loss to X = ₹2,400

So, 2 / 12 of total sum = 2,400

Total sum = 2,400 × 12 / 2

Total sum = ₹14,400
